chain: Decode the raw take with ffmpeg to float 44.1 kHz stereo (no normalisation, as qa.mjs does).

Cut [0, loopEnd), crossfade the last beat before loopEnd into the audio just before loopStart (equal power; the project's remaster.finish()) and append the 3 s run-on, an exact copy of the loop head. Loop points are exact samples. A take that opens with silence loses it first (`headTrimSeconds` in the cue's `master`).
One linear gain to -16.0 LUFS integrated (ffmpeg ebur128). No limiter was needed: the true peak after the gain is under the -1.5 dBFS ceiling.
Encode with libmp3lame -q:a 0 (V0), 44.1 kHz stereo, LAME/Info gapless header: the shipped music format.
No EQ, no stereo repair, no reverb, no exciter, no dither.
master.scripts: D:/Tools/elevenlabs/install/<cue>/tools (CAND=a|c|s python tools/11_master.py rebuilds the file); they import the project's own tools/audio/remaster.py from D:/pyrefly-elevenlabs (branch elevenlabs-groundwork).

stereoGate.result: Each cue's `themesStereoGate` says which of the three measures its installed file meets. The takes are wide and partly decorrelated, the image remaster R1 was built to repair, so most fail all three; the gate was written for renders of our own scores.
stereoGate.decision: The driver installed the `wide` variant of each cue, the stereo image Bailey picked by ear. The `narrow` variant is the same file with only the width stage added; it passes the gate. Swap with `node tools/audio/music-elevenlabs.mjs install --variant=narrow` then `measure`.

knownLimits: Band-limited at about 16.6 to 17.1 kHz. A take is a 128 kbps MP3 (the API default), so it carries a lowpass wall (a cliff of 27 to 44 dB, in `after.measure.cliff`) that our V0 encode keeps; the files they replace had 6 to 12 dB. Only a regeneration at a higher output format would remove it, and a new roll is a different piece of music.
The shipped file is a transcode: MP3 to float to MP3.

Not a render of the score. The score of each cue stays in src/audio/tracks as the synth fallback when the MP3 cannot load, and TRACK_NOTES and the cue map in docs/audio/THEMES.md still describe that score (its key, tempo and themes), not the take. No claim is made here that a take carries a motif of the thematic bible.
No resemblance check against existing music was run on any take (agents cannot hear, rule 13). The prompts name no composer, franchise, character or melody.
What Bailey said of each cue's loop jump is in its `pick`; no agent has heard anything.

Run on the release candidate's production build (dist-gate, BASE_PATH=/) on 2026-10-07: docs/audio/music-elevenlabs-2026-10-07-browser.json, summarised in `gates.browserProof`. The install notes record a headless Chromium 153 decode of each staged file equal to ffmpeg's (the sample counts in `after.decodedSamples`).
The two alternates (`alternates`) are encoded at LAME V4, the only cues that are not V0: the cap was not raised and V0 would not fit (their `master.why`).
supersedes: For each cue, the older record that last pinned its file: docs/audio/music-v2-2026-09-30.json (the FFX cues) or docs/audio/music-o1-2026-09-30.json (chapter-select). Their tests step aside for a cue this record lists, and the cue's `before` here is the file they pinned.
rollback: A cue's `before.manifestEntry` is its old manifest entry and `git show <base>:public/audio/music/<cue>.mp3` its old file (copies in D:/Tools/elevenlabs/install/<cue>/old/).

request.prompt: Gothic orchestral battle music at 132 BPM in C-sharp minor. A low pipe organ and double basses carry a slow, courteous, sinister six-note figure; staccato low strings and timpani drive a steady pulse; dark brass answers in long chords; a sustained wordless choir sings open vowels only, no words and no rhythmic chanting. It builds in three waves from a quiet organ and tolling bell to a full orchestra, with a hushed organ-only passage in the middle, and ends on a held tense chord. Elegant, menacing contempt, never frantic. Steady tempo, no tempo changes, no fade-out, no final cadence.

loop.how: Starts 4 ms before the downbeat attack at 7.3029 s (bar 5) and ends at the downbeat of bar 49, so the wrap is bar 48 (Eb) into bar 5 (D), the step the piece makes from bar 4 to bar 5. Bars 49 and 50, the final chord and its reverb tail are not in the loop.

request.prompt: Sparse, melancholy solo piano piece at 58 BPM in A minor. A lone flute plays four soft notes, then the piano answers with a slow rising phrase that never finishes, over gentle broken chords and one low string drone. Intimate, nostalgic, like a story that is already over being told anyway. Quiet dynamics, much silence and natural room reverb, no drums, no vocals. No fade-out; it ends unresolved on a held note.

notes: The stereo gate passes on the whole file by a hair (0.602, -6.0 dB, -1.0 dB against 0.60, -6, -1; unrounded 0.6021, -6.011, -0.971), and only because the 33 s flute opening is nearly mono. The loop body alone, which plays almost all the time, reads 0.469 / -4.3 / -1.36 and misses all three. The narrow variant passes on the whole file (0.726 / -7.9 / -0.6) and on the loop alone (0.626 / -6.3 / -0.92).

The take is in D minor (the brief asked for A minor) and its flute opening runs 33 s where the brief planned about 8 s, so the piano enters 33 s after the cue starts where the old file had it at 8 s; 33 s is a long time to sit on one soft line if a player lingers. The synth fallback (title.ts, A minor, 58 bpm) now plays a different piece from the file when the MP3 cannot load.
The raw take opens with 2.09 s of silence and qa.mjs allows 0.5 s, so the first 1.9 s were cut (83,790 samples; the cut part never exceeds -89.6 dBFS). TitleScreen fades the cue in over 1.6 s.

The wrap passes through the last chord's decay: about 2.5 s near -45 dBFS before the piano restarts at -21 dBFS. Of the loop's 100 ms blocks 3.4 % are under -40 dBFS and none under -50. It is a breath, not a stop, but it is the one place a listener could call a gap.
Band-limited at about 17.1 kHz (a 27 dB cliff); the music itself has almost nothing above 6 kHz, so the wall sits above what the piece uses.
